danville.jurisdiction: Town of Danville (a town, not a city), the Hendricks County seat. Wikipedia places it in Center and Washington townships. Town Hall is at 49 N. Wayne St.
danville.rental_rules: None found. The Danville Code of Ordinances (2025 S-13, current through Ord. 28-2024, passed 11-20-2024) has no rental registration, landlord registration, rental licensing, or rental inspection chapter; 'rental registration', 'rental unit' and 'landlord registration' return nothing, and every 'rental' hit is park-facility rentals, the fee schedule, the fair housing chapter (Ch. 98), or the smoke-detector rule. The UDO (adopted 2/7/2024) has no rental registration or inspection provision either. Rental-specific rules that do exist: Code 90.24 makes the owner, manager or rental agent of a dwelling unit responsible for installing and maintaining required smoke detectors (and any hard-wired detector), with the tenant responsible for batteries in battery-powered units the owner provides; Code 52.06(C) lets sewer charges be billed to the tenant unless the owner asks otherwise in writing, but the owner stays liable if the tenant doesn't pay, and the owner may inspect the town's collection records for the account.
danville.short_term_rentals: The UDO defines a short-term rental (per IC 36-1-24-6) as renting a single-family home, accessory dwelling, duplex, multi-family dwelling or condominium for less than 30 days at a time through a short-term rental platform. Table 2.1 lists 'short term rental' as 'S-S' (special exception, additional standards apply) in the R1, R2, R3, RU, CB-P and CB-S districts and does not list it in the other districts. Chapter 3 (Standards for Specific Uses) has no short-term rental section, so the 'additional standards' it points to were not found. A special exception is decided by the Board of Zoning Appeals.
danville.eviction_court: Hendricks County evictions (EV) are filed in Hendricks Superior Court No. 1, 3, 4, or 5, assigned on an even and random basis (local rule LR32-AR1 Rule 1(K), document marked 'Modified 12/16/25', posted by the county as 'Local Rules, effective January 1, 2026'). The courts sit at the Hendricks County Courthouse, 51 W. Main St., Danville, on the town's courthouse square.
danville.property_tax: Billed by the Hendricks County Treasurer (Danville); 2026 installments are due May 11 and November 10, with bills mailed once a year in late March or early April. The town's own FAQ confirms property taxes are handled by Hendricks County, not the town. As a non-homestead single-family home, a rental is capped at 2% of gross assessed value under IC 6-1.1-20.6-7.5, before any voter-approved referendum levies.

utilities.water: Town of Danville water utility (municipally owned; well water treated at the Danville Water Treatment Plant). Billed monthly by the Clerk-Treasurer's utility office at Town Hall: meters read around the 1st, bills mailed by the 15th, due the 4th of the following month, 10% penalty on the 5th, $50 disconnect/reconnection fee.
utilities.sewer: Town of Danville wastewater utility (plant at 1000 E. Broadway St., discharging to the West Fork of White Lick Creek), on the same town bill as water and stormwater. Under Code 52.06(C), sewer charges may be billed to the tenant unless the owner requests otherwise in writing; the owner remains liable for unpaid charges.
utilities.stormwater: Town stormwater utility, billed with water and wastewater by the Clerk-Treasurer.
utilities.account_setup: New water/sewer service is opened through the town's online 'Application for Water and Sewage Service' (one form of ID). An applicant who is not the deeded owner must give the owner's name and contact details, and the applicant affirms as either 'Owner of Record' or 'Tenant entered into rental agreement with the Owner of Record'. A $100 deposit applies: the online form says it is required of all renters and homeowners, while the code fee schedule (35.02) lists a $100 'Tenant: connection fee deposit - renters only'. All accounts carry a minimum monthly bill regardless of usage (Ords. 27-2023, 28-2023, 30-2023). Service is connected within 48 hours of processing, business hours only. No lease-copy requirement was found.
utilities.electric: Not a town utility (the town describes its utility as water and wastewater only). Provider by address not confirmed from an official source.
utilities.gas: Not confirmed from an official source.
utilities.trash: No town trash collection found: the code has no solid-waste collection chapter and the town's utility pages list only water, wastewater and stormwater. The town runs seasonal leaf collection and snow and ice control on its 53 miles of public roads. Whether residents must hire a private hauler was not confirmed from an official page.

danville.location: About 20 miles west of downtown Indianapolis along US 36, which is Danville's Main Street; SR 39 joins US 36 briefly in the center of town and runs north about 9 miles to I-74 at Lizton and south about 11 miles to I-70 (road figures per Wikipedia). The Hendricks County Courthouse anchors the historic courthouse square, and the UDO's Corridor Protection Overlay covers Main Street, US 36 and the blocks around the square. Danville Parks and Recreation maintains more than 165 acres across seven park sites, including Ellis Park, Gary Eakin Park, Jack Willard Park and Blanton Woods, plus more than 20 miles of paved and recreation trails, the 28,000 sq ft Danville Athletic Club and the Gill Family Aquatic Center. The Gordon Graham Airfield (Hendricks County Airport) has its own UDO overlay district.
unverified: Code currency: American Legal is current only through Ord. 28-2024 (11-20-2024), and Chapter 152 shows the zoning regulations last amended by Ord. 01-2024. Any 2025-2026 ordinance adding rental registration or STR standards would not show up there. Confirm with the Clerk-Treasurer or the Planning Department (317-745-4180 ext. 1101) before launch.

STR 'additional standards': Table 2.1 marks short-term rental 'S-S' but Chapter 3 of the posted UDO has no STR section. Either standards were added later or the table points to nothing. Confirm with Planning.

Legal question for counsel: IC 36-1-24-8 says zoning may not disallow an owner-occupied STR, and sec. 9 says a non-owner-occupied STR can need a special exception but cannot be effectively prohibited. Danville's table requires a special exception in all six districts where it lists the use and leaves STR out of the rest, without distinguishing owner-occupied. Don't present the special-exception requirement as applying to owner-occupied STRs.

UDO 3.02(B)(1) reads 'Approval of an accessory dwelling does permit the accessory dwelling to be used as a short-term rental', followed by a sentence requiring the STR use to be separately approved. This looks like a missing 'not'. Not quoted on the page.

Deposit wording conflict: the online application says the $100 deposit applies to 'all renters and homeowners', while the code fee schedule lists it as 'renters only'. Both agree a renter pays $100. An older PDF version of the application (2022) asked for two forms of ID and quoted a $59.73 minimum bill under Ord. 09-2020; it is superseded and not used.

Electric and gas providers: no official town or utility page naming them was found. The county-level HCEDP list (Duke Energy, Hendricks Power Cooperative, IMPA, Indianapolis Power & Light; Vectren/CenterPoint gas) from the earlier pass is not Danville-specific. Confirm with Duke Energy, Hendricks Power and CenterPoint territory lookups.

Trash: no town service was found, but no official page saying 'private haulers' was found either. Waste Management advertises residential service in Danville (third-party, not opened as a primary source).

Hendricks County 4-H Fairgrounds & Conference Complex at 1900 E. Main St., Danville: address appears in search results citing Purdue Extension handbooks, but no primary page was successfully opened (the 2025 handbook URL returned 404).

B&O Trail: TrailLink (third-party) lists a trail end at N. County Rd 250 E 'Danville'. Hendricks County Parks' own page did not say the B&O Trail or the Vandalia Trail reaches Danville, so neither is used. The Vandalia Trail sections described by the county are near Plainfield and Amo/Coatesville, not Danville.
SR 236: not confirmed from any source opened this pass, so it is left out of the location text.
Townships (Center and Washington) rest on Wikipedia only.

Hendricks County court allocation: the earlier pass noted proposed caseload-allocation amendments effective January 1, 2027. The county courts page checked today shows only the rules 'effective January 1, 2026' (document marked Modified 12/16/25) and no amendment notice. Re-check after January 1, 2027.
